about: Limits, placeholders and privacy patterns for loomi-connect-feedback. scripts/tool_feedback_report.py reads this file, so change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes. Names are compared normalised: lower case, with _, - and spaces removed (accountId and account_id are both accountid). Redaction is best effort; the final strings are linted exactly as sent: a hard leak blocks the plan's one change, a soft one is a warning shown in the confirmation, and the user reads every field before saying yes.

notes.max_field_chars: submit_llm_feedback's limit on feedback and on what_i_tried (from its schema). A longer field is a blocker: shorten it, don't let the tool cut it.
notes.summary_max_chars: The one-line summary may be at most this long, and must be one line. Longer is a blocker.
notes.gap_types: The values submit_llm_feedback's gap_type accepts (from its schema). Any other value is a blocker.
notes.completion_estimate_min: Lowest completion_estimate the tool accepts. The skill always sends one, because the tool's description asks for it.
notes.completion_estimate_max: Highest completion_estimate the tool accepts. The top value means the request was fully done, which a problem report rarely is, so it's a warning.
notes.environments: Allowed values of --environment. Required, with no default. Engagement has no staging environment, so staging on an Engagement report is a warning.
notes.products: Allowed values of the report's product field.
notes.min_seconds_between_reports: submit_llm_feedback's rate limit (from its description): at most one report in this many seconds. After a 429, wait at least this long, and the Retry-After time if longer.
notes.max_reports_per_hour: submit_llm_feedback's hourly limit (from its description). Another reason to send one chosen report, never a list.
notes.allowed_arg_keys: The only argument names (normalised) whose string values are kept in the reproduction, and only when the value matches plain_value_pattern: enum-like settings such as filter_preset or sort. Every other string becomes a placeholder named after its normalised key (<accountid>, <q>). Numbers, booleans and ISO dates are kept unless the name is sensitive or the number has min_numeric_id_digits or more digits.
notes.plain_value_pattern: A kept argument value must match this: lower-case tokens, optionally separated by single spaces or commas (price desc, pid,brand). No capitals, digits runs, slashes or @.
notes.excerpt_text_keys: In a response excerpt that parses as JSON, strings under these names (error and message text) are kept after free-text redaction, because they usually show the problem. Every other string becomes a placeholder.
notes.sensitive_name_words: A name (argument, JSON key, or name: value / name=value / name == value / name in value pair in text, the name may start with _) whose normalised form contains one of these is sensitive: its value is replaced, numbers and dates included (a date under a birth or dob key is replaced).
notes.sensitive_name_suffixes: A normalised name ending with one of these is sensitive too (accountid, customerids, lastmodifiedby, clientip).
notes.sensitive_names_exact: Normalised names that are sensitive only as a whole word (q, ip, dob, zip, aov): as substrings they'd match too much.
notes.context_id_words: In free text, a value right after one of these words that contains a digit or a hyphen, underscore or dot (customer 12, user jane-d) is replaced by <word>.
notes.person_context_words: In free text, capitalised words right after one of these (User Jane Doe, reported by Zoë) are replaced by <name>. A lower-case word there that isn't in name_stopwords is a soft warning.
notes.token_patterns: Regular expressions for well-known secret token formats (cloud keys, OAuth tokens, payment, chat and code-host tokens). Replaced by <token>, and a hard block if any are left.
notes.host_tlds: A dotted name ending in one of these, or in any two-letter country code, or starting with www, is a host: replaced by <host>, and a hard block if left. Other dotted names (data.debug) are a soft warning. Hosts with a scheme or a path are always <url>.
notes.min_hex_id_chars: A run of at least this many hexadecimal characters with both a letter and a digit, or any UUID, counts as an ID and is replaced by <id>.
notes.min_numeric_id_digits: A run of at least this many digits counts as an ID and is replaced by <id>, in text and in arguments. A hard block if any are left.
notes.min_phone_digits: Digits written with separators (spaces, dots, brackets, hyphens) or a leading + that add up to at least this many count as a phone number (<phone>). Dates are left alone.
notes.min_opaque_token_chars: A run of at least this many letters, digits, _, -, /, + or = with both letters and digits is an unrecognised token or ID: a hard block.
notes.repo_doc_url: Public URL of docs/known-tool-behaviour.md. The report links to #L<line> of it when the problem comes from that file. This URL, with an optional #L<number>, is the only URL allowed in a report.
notes.known_marker: The text that marks an item in docs/known-tool-behaviour.md as worth reporting. list-known lists the lines that carry it, and build refuses a known_line without it.
notes.known_excerpt_chars: How much of the known-behaviour line (and its parent bullet) is quoted in the report.
notes.report_prefix: Start of the feedback text, so the Loomi Connect team can tell reports sent with this skill from others.
notes.name_stopwords: Words after a trigger word (by, user, name...) that aren't names, so 'sorted by date' isn't flagged.
notes.known_phrases: Capitalised phrases that are product or event names, not people or customers: never a soft warning.
notes.not_host_suffixes: Last parts of a dotted name that make it a file name or field path, not a host (data.json, customer.id).
notes.map_parent_keys: In a JSON excerpt or arguments, every key of an object under one of these (normalised) is replaced: such keys are data (search terms, facet values).
notes.map_parent_prefixes: Same as map_parent_keys, for parents whose normalised name starts with one of these (top_queries, topBrands).
notes.max_object_keys: An object with more keys than this is treated as a map of data, and every key is replaced.
notes.currency_codes: Currency codes that make a number next to them a money amount: a soft warning.
notes.business_metric_words: A number within a few words after one of these is a business figure: a soft warning, because the user may not want to share it.
notes.private_terms_none_line: The private terms file must list names, or hold this line to say none were used in the session; an empty file blocks the plan.
notes.context_any_words: In free text, ANY number or token right after one of these (acct 6012, site 7, domain key acme_us_en) is replaced by <word>, unless the token is in context_stopwords. A hard block if left.
notes.context_stopwords: Words after a context_any_words word that aren't IDs or names, so 'site search' and 'account and project' stay readable.
notes.common_capitalised_words: Capitalised words that aren't names: a pair made only of these isn't a warning, and they're ignored inside quoted strings.
notes.known_field_names: Field and parameter names with several _ or - parts that aren't data, so they don't raise the separated_token warning (tool names come from --published-tools).
notes.known_arg_values: Known values for allow-listed argument keys (normalised key). A kept value with an underscore-joined part not listed here (status acme_vip_list) is a soft warning; for a field_list_keys key, every field not listed is.
notes.field_list_keys: Allow-listed keys whose value is a comma list of field names: any field not in known_arg_values is a soft warning.
